name: Inlaod Itneg
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

new_statements.quote: Its phonology is conservative, with 14 consonants, four vowels, phonemic stress, and common morphophonemic processes.
new_statements.citation: Gonzales, Ryn Jean Fe V. 2025. A Grammar of Itneg Inlaud [Unpublished doctoral dissertation, Department of Linguistics, University of the Philippines Diliman]. Abstract in: The Archive (UP Department of Linguistics) 6(2): 199-200.
new_statements.locator: Abstract, The Archive 6(2) p. 200 (second paragraph on that page); same text on https://linguistics.upd.edu.ph/theses_dissertation/a-grammar-of-itneg-inlaud/
new_statements.rule_in_words: The author's abstract says only that stress is phonemic (contrastive), i.e. its position is not predictable from the segmental string; the abstract gives no position rule. The two SIL Inlaod/Binongan wordlists on file mark stress per word on either the penult or the final syllable, consistent with lexical stress, but they state no rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Abstract-level claim about the phonology of the language as a whole; no word/phrase domain discussion available. The full dissertation (ten chapters, includes the sound system) is unpublished and not online.
new_statements.identity_note: Target is Inlaod (Inlaud, western) Itneg, iti / inla1260. Himes 1997 (p. 103) treats Itneg as one language with two dialects, Binongan (eastern, itb / bino1237) and Inlaod (western). The only published phonemic sketch (Walton in Reid 1971) and Walton 1975 describe Binongan, not Inlaod; the SIL Binongan wordlist held on file is bino1237 material. Gonzales 2025 and the SIL Danglas wordlist are Inlaod proper (Danglas, Lagangilang, Peñarrubia, Langiden area).

sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey); publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Itneg phonology' (p. 107) treats only segments (four-vowel system, /o/ for *u, diphthong reflexes); PKI inventory lists *V: (length) but nothing on stress placement in Itneg. Confirms Binongan and Inlaod as the two Itneg dialects (p. 103).

sources.citation: Walton, Charles. 1966. Itneg - Binongan Wordlist (1966 Expanded Philippine Word List). SIL archive item 80568; the SIL record says the list plus a brief phonemic sketch was published in Reid (ed.) 1971. [Binongan Itneg = bino1237, not the target]
sources.note: Typed list marks stress with an apostrophe before the stressed syllable, both penult and final (qaba'ka, gi'dam, 'qobit, 'balat, bo'wa, mag'laga, 'laqod); the phonemic sketch is not in this PDF; no rule stated.
